- A new line was added to the `modify_p4d_table` function:
  - `p4d_populate(&init_mm, p4d, pud);` was added after the allocation of the `pud` entry. This line ensures that the newly allocated `pud` entry is properly linked to the `p4d` entry, which is necessary for the correct functioning of 4-level paging.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification in `vmem.c` addresses a bug related to the handling of 4-level paging in the kernel. By adding the `p4d_populate` function call, the patch ensures that the newly allocated page upper directory (PUD) is correctly associated with the page four directory (P4D). This fix prevents kernel crashes that occur when 4-level paging is utilized, thereby enhancing the stability and reliability of the memory management system in the kernel.

        Commit message:
        s390/vmem: fix vmem_add_range for 4-level paging

The kernel currently crashes if 4-level paging is used. Add missing
p4d_populate for just allocated pud entry.

Fixes: 3e0d3e408e63 ("s390/vmem: consolidate vmem_add_range() and vmem_remove_range()")
Reviewed-by: Gerald Schaefer <gerald.schaefer@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Vasily Gorbik <gor@linux.ibm.com>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/arch/s390/mm/vmem.c b/arch/s390/mm/vmem.c
index 1aed1a4dfc2d..eddf71c22875 100644
--- a/arch/s390/mm/vmem.c
+++ b/arch/s390/mm/vmem.c
@@ -402,6 +402,7 @@ static int modify_p4d_table(pgd_t *pgd, unsigned long addr, unsigned long end,
 			pud = vmem_crst_alloc(_REGION3_ENTRY_EMPTY);
 			if (!pud)
 				goto out;
+			p4d_populate(&init_mm, p4d, pud);
 		}
 		ret = modify_pud_table(p4d, addr, next, add, direct);
 		if (ret)
